purge.label: Trash purge and sync-oplog prune
purge.why: Every peer must run this itself: pruneSyncOps only ever prunes the oplog of the instance it runs on. The hard deletes are the same decision from the same data on every peer, and deleting an already-deleted row is a no-op.

relatedness.label: Relatedness cache refresh
relatedness.why: item_relatedness is a per-instance cache, deliberately outside ADR-206's synced-table list, so a local peer's Discover and Loose Ends stay empty until it computes its own. Two peers filling their own caches is not a conflict.

agent-purge.label: Claude in Ledgr cleanup
agent-purge.why: In-app agent chats are hub-local tables outside the synced set, so each machine clears its own expired side chats and old records. A peer without the agent has nothing to delete, which is a no-op.

snapshot.label: Local snapshots (restore points)
snapshot.why: Purely local: it dumps THIS peer's own cluster to THIS peer's own disk, so two peers snapshotting is two independent backups rather than a conflict. SCHEDULED here, but switched on in the app (ADR-222): the endpoint asks `snapshots:enabled` and returns without dumping when the owner has not turned restore points on, which is the default. Scheduling it always is what lets that switch be a checkbox instead of a config edit and a restart.
notes: timeoutMs: a dump of a real database takes longer than an API call; the default 120s ceiling would report a false failure and leave a partial file.

export.label: OneDrive export
export.why: One OneDrive folder. Two peers writing it would fight over the files and over items.exported_at — so the endpoint runs only on the copy named under Scheduled work, and stands down everywhere else. Scheduled here always so that naming this machine is all it takes (ADR-225).
export.what: Writes a copy of everything to OneDrive as plain files. That copy is what you would open if the internet were down.
export.consequence: A backup that runs late is harmless: the next run catches up on everything that changed.

calendar-sync.label: Calendar sync
calendar-sync.why: Creates items from Graph events. Two peers matching the same event would create two rows and sync would propagate both — so the endpoint runs only on the copy named under Scheduled work. Scheduled here always (ADR-225).
calendar-sync.what: Turns your calendar events into meeting records here.
calendar-sync.consequence: Meetings already brought in stay correct everywhere. The list of meetings waiting to be added only refreshes on the machine that runs it.
notes: movable, PROVEN 2026-08-25 (ADR-221): "have I already made a record for this event?" is answered from items.ms_event_id, which syncs, so a new owner cannot make a second copy of a meeting. Each run pulls the whole window fresh, and calendar_events is a per-copy cache a new owner refills on its first run (verify-calendar-sync.mts proves it).

email-import.label: Email-in
email-import.why: Consumes the mailbox: whichever peer reads a message first is the only one that sees it — so the endpoint runs only on the copy named under Scheduled work. Scheduled here always (ADR-225).
email-import.what: Turns messages you forward into items here.
email-import.consequence: Nothing is missed while it waits. A forwarded message stays in the folder until it has been brought in.
notes: movable, PROVEN 2026-08-25 (ADR-221): what consumes a message is MOVING it out of the pickup folder, which happens in the mailbox where every copy sees it, so a new owner lists exactly the messages nobody has brought in yet. items.properties.email.internetMessageId syncs as a second guard (verify-email-in.mts hands the job over mid-flight and proves it).

todoist-sync.label: Todoist sync
todoist-sync.why: Bidirectional against one Todoist account. Two peers pushing the same tasks is the classic double-write.
todoist-sync.what: Keeps tasks in step with Todoist, in both directions.
todoist-sync.blocked: Moving this needs one check first: it writes to Todoist as well as reading from it.

transcription-poll.label: Transcription poll
transcription-poll.why: Claims transcription jobs from the provider; two pollers race for the same job.
transcription-poll.what: Collects finished transcripts of meeting recordings.
transcription-poll.blocked: Moving this needs one check first: two machines would race for the same job.

youtube-transcript.label: Video transcripts
youtube-transcript.why: Writes the transcript into the saved link itself. Two machines transcribing the same video would both write the same body and then fight over whose copy wins, so the endpoint runs only on the copy named under Scheduled work, and stands down everywhere else. Scheduled here always so that naming this machine is all it takes (ADR-225).
youtube-transcript.what: Writes the words spoken in a saved video into the saved link, so you can read and search them here.
youtube-transcript.consequence: A late run costs nothing. A video simply waits until the machine that does this picks it up, however long that takes.
notes: No timeoutMs on purpose: the endpoint starts the work and answers immediately, because Node destroys any request left open for five minutes. A 30-minute ceiling it once carried could never be reached and only made the scheduler wait five minutes to hear "fetch failed" about work that was going fine (first real run, 2026-08-31).

movable from the day it shipped: the waiting list is worked out fresh each run (saved videos with no transcript yet), and the done mark lives in the video body, which syncs. A machine without the transcribing tools says so on Build rather than failing quietly.

health-check.label: Weekly health check
health-check.why: Pushes to the owner's devices. Per-instance push subscriptions a local peer does not have, and it would double the alert where it does.
health-check.what: Looks everything over once a week and notifies you only if something needs attention.
health-check.blocked: Moving this needs one check first: notifications are registered per machine, so it would reach different devices.
